item.title: Israeli shelling hits south Lebanon minutes after ceasefire takes effect
item.description:
Less than an hour after a 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon officially went into effect on Thursday evening, fresh shelling struck towns in southern Lebanon, casting immediate doubt over the durability of the truce.

Lebanon's National News Agency reported that Israeli artillery continued to shell the towns of Khiam and Dibbine after the 5 p.m. ET (21:00 GMT) deadline passed, with sweeping operations involving machine-gun fire also reported in the area. The Israeli military simultaneously warned residents of southern Lebanon not to move south of the Litani River, stating that its forces remain deployed there.

item.title: Trump warns U.S. 'won't be there' for Italy over airbase denial
item.description:
President Donald Trump escalated his feud with Italy on Wednesday, posting on Truth Social that "Italy wasn't there for us, we won't be there for them!" — a sharp warning directed at one of Washington's closest European allies over Rome's refusal to allow U.S. military aircraft to use the Sigonella airbase in Sicily for operations linked to the ongoing war in Iran.

The post, which linked to a Guardian report on the incident, caps weeks of deteriorating relations between Trump and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, once considered Europe's most reliable bridge to the White House.

item.title: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire takes effect as gold rises on peace hopes
item.description: Gold prices rose on Thursday as the U.S. dollar weakened, with investors growing optimistic that diplomatic progress in the Middle East — including a newly announced ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon and the prospect of renewed U.S.-Iran negotiations — could ease the geopolitical pressures that have roiled markets for weeks.

item.title: Oil prices fall as Trump announces Israel-Lebanon ceasefire
item.description: Oil prices retreated on Thursday after President Donald Trump expressed optimism about the prospect of ending the war with Iran, even as the broader energy market remained on edge over continued disruptions in the Persian Gulf.

item.title: Starmer and Macron host 40-nation summit on reopening Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
British Prime Minister Keir Starmer is set to arrive in Paris on Friday to co-host a summit with French President Emmanuel Macron aimed at restoring freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, the critical waterway that carries roughly 20% of the world's oil supply. Around 40 countries are expected to join the virtual meeting, which Downing Street described as advancing "a coordinated, independent, multinational plan to safeguard international shipping once the conflict ends".

Starmer is expected to tell the gathering that "the unconditional and immediate reopening of the Strait is a global responsibility," urging international leaders to act collectively to get "global energy and trade flowing freely again". The initiative, formally called the Strait of Hormuz Maritime Freedom of Navigation Initiative, will focus on supporting the fragile ceasefire in the region and developing plans for mine clearance and military assurance for commercial shipping.

item.title: Iran war drives nuclear power surge across Asia and Africa
item.description:
The energy shock unleashed by the 2026 Iran war is pushing nations across Asia and Africa to ramp up nuclear power generation and accelerate long-dormant atomic energy plans, as countries scramble to insulate themselves from the worst oil and gas disruption in modern history.

The effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz — the chokepoint for roughly 20% of the world's crude oil and liquefied natural gas — has cut off fuel supplies that Asian economies in particular depend on, according to the Associated Press. African and Asian nations that already operate nuclear plants are boosting output for immediate relief, while countries without reactors are fast-tracking development programs that could take decades to bear fruit but may reshape energy policy for a generation.

item.title: Asian stocks near pre-war levels as oil drops on ceasefire hopes
item.description: Asian equities were on track for a second consecutive week of gains and oil prices held below $100 a barrel on Friday, as growing optimism over a potential extension of the U.S.-Iran ceasefire buoyed investor sentiment across global markets.

item.title: Strait of Hormuz sees more ships despite US blockade
item.description: The Iran war's closure of the Strait of Hormuz — described by the International Energy Agency as the "largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market" — is reshaping energy policy across Asia and Africa, driving nations toward nuclear power and alternative crude suppliers as fossil fuel flows from the Gulf remain choked nearly seven weeks after hostilities began.

item.title: Thousands of displaced Lebanese head south as ceasefire takes hold
item.description: Thousands of displaced Lebanese families surged onto highways heading south on Friday, hours after a 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah took effect at midnight local time, halting weeks of devastating conflict that killed more than 2,100 people and uprooted over a million from their homes.

item.title: Trump says Iran deal is close as Lebanon ceasefire takes hold
item.description:
President Donald Trump expressed confidence on Thursday that a deal to end the war with Iran is within reach, as a new 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon went into effect and diplomatic channels intensified ahead of a critical deadline next week.

"I think we're very close to making a deal with Iran," Trump told reporters outside the White House on Thursday. Speaking later in Las Vegas, he went further, saying the war "should be ending pretty soon". Trump indicated that a second round of in-person talks between the United States and Iran could take place as soon as this weekend in Islamabad, Pakistan, and said he might travel there himself if an agreement is signed.

item.title: Kyushu researchers produce hydrogen from alcohol using iron and UV light
item.description: Researchers at Kyushu University in Japan have discovered a remarkably simple method for producing hydrogen gas by combining iron ions with methanol and sodium hydroxide, then exposing the mixture to ultraviolet light. The findings, published in Communications Chemistry on April 17, represent a potential step toward cheaper and more sustainable hydrogen production.

item.title: European markets tread water ahead of weekend US-Iran talks
item.description: European stock markets traded in a narrow range on Friday as investors adopted a cautious stance ahead of a potentially pivotal weekend of diplomacy between the United States and Iran. The pan-European STOXX 600 was subdued but on track to notch its fourth consecutive weekly gain, buoyed by lingering hopes that the conflict in the Middle East may be approaching a resolution.

item.title: NASA picks Falcon Heavy to launch ESA's Mars rover in 2028
item.description:
NASA announced Thursday that it has approved the start of implementation for its contributions to the European Space Agency's long-delayed Rosalind Franklin Mars rover, selecting SpaceX's Falcon Heavy rocket to carry the mission to the Red Planet no earlier than late 2028.

The approval moves the Rosalind Franklin Support and Augmentation (ROSA) project from the design phase into full implementation, a step that had been in question amid ongoing budget pressures from the Trump administration. The rover, if it launches on schedule, would arrive at Mars in 2030.

item.title: IATA warns Europe could see flight cancellations by late May amid jet fuel shortage
item.description:
European flights could begin to be cancelled from the end of May due to dwindling jet fuel supplies, the International Air Transport Association warned on Friday, as the closure of the Strait of Hormuz continues to choke the continent's primary fuel supply route.

IATA Director General Willie Walsh said the airline industry body's own estimates point to cancellations starting within weeks. "By the end of May we could start to see some cancellations in Europe for lack of jet fuel," Walsh said. The warning came a day after Fatih Birol, executive director of the International Energy Agency, told the Associated Press that Europe has "maybe six weeks or so of jet fuel left," calling the crisis "the largest energy crisis we have ever faced".

item.title: Iran declares Strait of Hormuz open to all ships during ceasefire
item.description: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared the Strait of Hormuz "completely open" to all commercial vessels on Friday, linking the move to the 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon that took effect at midnight local time. The announcement marks the first time since the war began on February 28 that Tehran has offered unrestricted commercial passage through the waterway.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV draws massive crowd at Douala Mass
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass before a crowd expected to number 600,000 at Japoma Stadium in Douala, Cameroon, on Friday, marking the largest gathering of his 11-day apostolic journey across Africa. The Vatican had predicted the turnout would be the biggest of the tour, though reports from the ground suggested attendance may have fallen short of projections due to extreme heat and tight security.

The liturgy in Cameroon's economic capital came on the pontiff's third day in the country, part of a broader April 13–23 tour that began in Algeria and will continue to Angola and Equatorial Guinea. It is the first time an American pope has visited the African continent.

item.title: US delays weapons deliveries to European allies as Iran war strains stockpiles
item.description:
The United States has informed several European allies that previously contracted weapons deliveries will likely be delayed as the war with Iran continues to deplete American military stockpiles, Reuters reported on Wednesday, citing five sources familiar with the matter.

Countries in the Baltic region and Scandinavia — some of which share a border with Russia — are among those affected, with delays hitting systems purchased under the Foreign Military Sales program that have not yet been delivered. U.S. officials communicated the expected postponements in bilateral messages to European counterparts in recent days, the sources said.

item.title: Oil plunges as Iran opens Strait of Hormuz to shipping
item.description:
Oil prices tumbled sharply on Friday after Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared the Strait of Hormuz "completely open" to all commercial vessels for the duration of the ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon, sending crude to its lowest levels in five weeks and fueling a broad rally on Wall Street.

Brent crude fell roughly 10%, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate also dropped by double digits, according to CNN. The sell-off marked the steepest single-day decline since early April, when the initial U.S.-Iran ceasefire announcement sent prices plunging more than 15%.

item.title: Trump keeps naval blockade despite Iran reopening Hormuz
item.description: President Trump declared on Friday that the U.S. naval blockade on Iran will remain in place even after Tehran announced it was reopening the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping, setting up a tense final stretch of negotiations before the ceasefire expires on April 22.

item.title: Iran war reshapes global energy policy as nations fast-track renewables
item.description:
The escalating conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran — now in its seventh week — is reshaping global energy policy, as countries exposed to the largest oil supply disruption in decades accelerate their pivot toward renewable power.

Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly 20% of the world's oil and gas supply transits, has locked an estimated 13 million barrels of oil per day out of global markets. A U.S. military blockade of Iranian ports, ordered by President Donald Trump on Monday after ceasefire talks collapsed, has further choked the waterway. The twin disruptions have pushed crude prices near historic highs and laid bare the vulnerabilities of fossil fuel dependency.
